item.title: Power Bills, Travel Deals and Digital Access Shift
item.description: Electricity pricing, Australian travel costs, finance infrastructure and useful digital services changed in concrete ways.
item.content:encoded:
Electricity pricing, Australian travel costs, finance infrastructure and useful digital services changed in concrete ways.

  1. NZ low-user electricity plans end next April The Electricity Authority says retailers will no longer be required to offer low fixed-charge plans from 1 April 2027, and has told distributors to manage and disclose the consumer impact of repricing. 22 Sep 2026. Electricity Authority · Follow up
  2. Victoria sets tougher rules for new data centres Victoria announced rules for future data centres requiring their own renewable-energy supply and storage, self-funded grid connections, non-potable cooling water and location restrictions near homes and schools. 22 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  3. Jetstar staff will waive baggage and seat fees About 1,000 Jetstar customer-service staff plan industrial action on 23–24 September that keeps passenger service running while waiving excess-baggage, seat-change and other fees at major Australian airports. 22 Sep 2026. The Australian · Follow up
  4. Qantas offers 30% off domestic base fares for visitors Qantas launched an Explorer promotion offering international travellers 30% off base fares, excluding taxes and charges, to more than 45 Australian domestic destinations. 22 Sep 2026. The Australian · Follow up
  5. Googlebook launches with Australian retail availability Google launched its new premium Googlebook laptop line from US$899, with retail availability scheduled for 4–5 October in Australia and several other markets. 21 Sep 2026. Indian Express · Follow up
  6. ECB launches central-bank-money settlement for tokenised assets The Eurosystem launched Pontes, allowing wholesale tokenised-asset transactions to settle in central-bank money; Deutsche Bank, Santander and Clearstream are among initial participants. 21 Sep 2026. ECB · Follow up
  7. Amazon blocks Meta Muse from shopping on Amazon Amazon is blocking Meta's Muse AI agent from accessing its marketplace, so Muse users cannot currently use the agent to shop on Amazon. 22 Sep 2026. Business Insider · Follow up
  8. Gmail search AI Overviews expand globally Google expanded Gmail Search AI Overviews from the US to global paid-plan users with Gmail set to English; the feature answers natural-language questions across email when Workspace smart features are enabled. 15 Sep 2026. Google · Follow up
  9. ChatGPT is now available inside Microsoft Word OpenAI released a ChatGPT add-in for Microsoft Word across all ChatGPT plans, adding drafting, summarisation, revision and formatting from a Word sidebar. 17 Sep 2026. OpenAI · Follow up
  10. Wellington gets a free citywide giant-bee art trail Bee in the City opened with 30 giant artist-designed sculptures plus 20 community bees from the airport through the waterfront and central city to the Botanic Garden, running until 8 November. 14 Sep 2026. Wellington News · Follow up
  11. Wellington will get a new immersive WOW exhibition A new high-tech World of WearableArt exhibition will premiere in Wellington in 2027, backed by NZ$880,000 from the Major Events Fund and planned to run alongside the annual WOW season. 17 Sep 2026. Beehive · Follow up
  12. Marian Maguire's Labyrinth opens in central Wellington Bowen Galleries opened Marian Maguire's Labyrinth exhibition at 39 Ghuznee Street today; it runs through 10 October. 22 Sep 2026. Bowen Galleries · Follow up
  13. Westpac changes multiple NZ mortgage rates this week RateMate's 22 September snapshot records Westpac increasing 12 mortgage-rate terms and cutting two since 17 September; its listed two-year special is 5.29%. 22 Sep 2026. RateMate · Follow up
  14. Australian banks lift fixed mortgage rates before the RBA meeting Commonwealth Bank raised its two-year fixed home-loan rate by 0.48 percentage points and Westpac lifted fixed rates by up to 0.45 points, with NAB and ANZ also recently increasing rates. 22 Sep 2026. Courier Mail · Follow up
  15. Sydney bans smart glasses in municipal facilities The City of Sydney has prohibited smart glasses in municipal facilities, adding a concrete local restriction on camera-equipped wearables in public spaces. 22 Sep 2026. Guardian · Follow up
  16. New Android banking malware uses AI for device control Zimperium identified RedHat, an Android banking trojan distributed outside Google Play that abuses Accessibility permissions, overlays banking apps and uses image analysis to adapt its on-screen control; avoiding sideloaded apps and denying unexpected Accessibility access blocks its main route. 19 Sep 2026. TechRadar · Follow up
  17. Australian petrol and diesel prices jump sharply Australian regular unleaded is averaging about A$2.38 a litre and diesel about A$2.84, materially raising driving costs for anyone travelling or relocating there. 22 Sep 2026. Daily Telegraph · Follow up
  18. Starship's first orbital attempt moves to 28 September SpaceX postponed Starship Flight 14 from 22 to 28 September; the mission remains planned as Starship's first orbital flight and first deployment of 26 operational V3 Starlink satellites. 18 Sep 2026. Investors.com · Follow up

item.title: Payments, Privacy and Travel Conditions Shift
item.description: Payment rules, privacy enforcement, travel conditions and market access changed in concrete ways.
item.content:encoded:
Payment rules, privacy enforcement, travel conditions and market access changed in concrete ways.

  1. Australia’s card-surcharge ban starts 1 October Visa, Mastercard, American Express and eftpos card networks will prohibit card surcharges in Australia from 1 October, covering in-store and online card payments. 21 Sep 2026. Guardian · Follow up
  2. Vietnam floods inundate more than 16,000 homes Flooding across northern and central Vietnam has inundated more than 16,000 homes and left roads and low-lying areas submerged, materially disrupting travel in affected provinces. 19 Sep 2026. AP · Follow up
  3. Bank of Japan raises rate to 1.25% The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate from 1.00% to 1.25%, its highest level since 1995. 21 Sep 2026. News.com.au · Follow up
  4. Google fined €403 million over location-data processing Ireland’s Data Protection Commission fined Google €403 million after an inquiry into its processing of location data. 21 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  5. US SEC opens five-year path for tokenized stocks The US Securities and Exchange Commission created a five-year exemption for qualifying tokenized-stock trading while requiring the tokens to carry the same shareholder rights as the underlying shares. 17 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  6. Wellington approves second central-city bus corridor Wellington City Council approved the Harbour Quays bus-priority project, with a new two-way waterfront bus corridor, new or upgraded stops and implementation work expected to begin in 2027. 17 Sep 2026. Metlink · Follow up
  7. Pixel September update adds faster VIP contacts Google began rolling out the September Pixel Drop to Pixel 6 and newer phones, adding one-tap VIP contact actions and notification badges; Pixel Watch 3 and newer also gain expanded one-handed notification gestures. 15 Sep 2026. Android Authority · Follow up
  8. Android adds remembered-item tracking without a tag Google’s September Android Drop lets supported Android 16+ devices save where untagged items such as passports or spare keys were placed in Find Hub, with optional photos. 1 Sep 2026. Google · Follow up
  9. Fabric SQL editor upgrades reach general availability Microsoft Fabric’s September release moved SQL query-editor enhancements to general availability, including a faster results grid, scalable object explorer, IntelliSense, autosave controls and SQL file import/export. Sep 2026. Microsoft Learn · Follow up
  10. Gemini 3.8 Live models launch for real-time voice Google launched Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking for real-time voice-agent workloads, with the new models also feeding voice capabilities across Google products. 16 Sep 2026. Times of India · Follow up
  11. Australian wholesale power prices fall sharply Wholesale electricity prices in Australia fell 21% to 43% year-on-year across states in the September quarter, reducing the wholesale component feeding future retail electricity costs. 21 Sep 2026. The Australian · Follow up
  12. China slows humanoid-robot IPO pipeline Chinese regulators have used informal guidance to slow some humanoid-robot listings after volatile trading in the sector, tightening the near-term pipeline for a heavily funded investment theme. 21 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  13. Trafigura launches 14-tanker Volare unit Trafigura launched Volare Shipping with six operating supertankers and eight more on order, and plans a private placement followed by an Oslo listing around 5 October. 21 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  14. Yuan reaches strongest level since January 2023 China’s onshore yuan strengthened to 6.6957 per US dollar, its strongest level in more than three and a half years. 21 Sep 2026. Reuters via MarketScreener · Follow up
  15. Typhoon Dujuan disrupts travel in eastern Japan Typhoon Dujuan brought heavy rain and landslide warnings to eastern Japan, including the Kanto region, and disrupted scheduled events and travel movements. 21 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  16. Fed and BoE probe bank exposure after Jane Street loss The US Federal Reserve and Bank of England are collecting information on banks’ exposure and risk controls around major trading firms after Jane Street sustained a reported $15 billion loss. 21 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  17. Four Chinese companies launch Hong Kong offerings Four Chinese companies launched or prepared Hong Kong share offerings seeking up to HK$14.35 billion in total, with trading scheduled to begin on 29 September. 20 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  18. AFL final drives exceptional Melbourne airfares Return economy fares from Perth and Brisbane to Melbourne surged into the thousands of Australian dollars for grand-final week even after airlines added thousands of extra seats. 21 Sep 2026. The Australian · Follow up
